programs.name: Distribution and Logistics Warehouse Financing
programs.description: Class A and Class B distribution warehouses, logistics facilities, and e-commerce fulfillment centers. The largest industrial sub-class by deal volume and the most competitively financed.
typical_stack: Permanent loan: life insurance company, CMBS, or bank
Construction loan: bank or debt fund for ground-up distribution
Bridge: debt fund for transitional or repositioning plays
Agency overlay on flex industrial or MF-adjacent

key_features.building_specs: Clear heights 32+ ft, ESFR sprinklers, dock doors, trailer parking, truck courts
key_features.most_competitive_lender: Life insurance companies for stabilized with credit tenancy
key_features.ltv_ranges: 65 to 70 percent life co, 70 to 75 percent CMBS, 75 to 80 percent bank owner-user
key_features.rate_environment_2026: Life co 150 to 200 over 10-year, CMBS 200 to 300 over, bank 175 to 275 over

seo.meta_template: Distribution and logistics warehouse financing in {city}. Lender ecosystem, underwriting criteria, and capital stack for Class A and Class B distribution assets.

programs.name: Cold Storage and Refrigerated Warehouse Financing
programs.description: Refrigerated and frozen warehouse facilities serving food distribution, 3PL cold chain, grocery wholesalers, and pharmaceutical cold storage. Specialty sub-class requiring lenders who understand refrigeration CapEx.
typical_stack: Permanent loan: life insurance company with specialty industrial desk, CMBS for large stabilized portfolios
Construction loan: specialty bank or debt fund with cold chain experience
Bridge: debt funds for value-add cold storage repositioning

key_features.development_cost_premium: Refrigerated buildings cost $250 to $400/sf vs $100 to $150/sf for dry warehouse
key_features.tenant_profile: National cold chain operators (3PLs), food distributors, grocery wholesalers
key_features.infrastructure: Refrigeration systems, insulation, backup power, temperature-controlled receiving, ammonia or synthetic refrigerants
key_features.cap_rate_premium_vs_dry: Typically 50 to 100 bps wider than Class A dry warehouse
key_features.environmental_considerations: Ammonia refrigeration triggers specific environmental disclosures

seo.title_suffix: Cold Storage and Refrigerated Warehouse Financing
seo.meta_template: Cold storage and refrigerated warehouse financing in {city}. Specialty industrial lenders, refrigeration CapEx underwriting, and capital stack for cold chain facilities.

programs.name: Data Center Financing
programs.description: Hyperscale, colocation, and enterprise data center facilities. Specialty sub-class with strong institutional demand, backed by credit-tenant lease structures and hardened power and connectivity infrastructure.
programs.typical_deal_range: $15M to $500M+ depending on facility tier and capacity
typical_stack: Permanent loan: life insurance company with data center specialty desk, CMBS for stabilized hyperscale-leased assets
Construction loan: specialty data center debt fund or bank with expertise
Specialty REIT lending for portfolio and credit-tenant structures

key_features.tenant_structures: Hyperscale (build-to-suit, investment grade credit, 10-15 year NNN), colocation operator credit, enterprise self-operated
key_features.development_cost: Shell $250 to $400/sf plus power and cooling infrastructure $500 to $1,500/sf depending on tier and density
key_features.key_underwriting: Tenant credit, power commitment agreements, fiber connectivity, cooling redundancy, tier classification
key_features.top_markets: Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, Phoenix, Atlanta, Chicago
key_features.2026_tailwind: AI and hyperscale demand driving unprecedented capital deployment

seo.meta_template: Data center financing in {city}. Hyperscale and colocation lender appetite, tenant credit underwriting, and capital stack for data center real estate.

programs.name: Manufacturing and Heavy Industrial Financing
programs.description: Single-purpose manufacturing facilities, heavy industrial campuses, food processing, specialty production. Lenders decline most of these deals because they can't underwrite single-purpose buildings, specialty equipment, or environmental overlays.
typical_stack: Permanent loan: life insurance company with industrial specialty desk for stabilized with credit tenancy
SBA 504 or 7(a) for qualifying owner-user manufacturing (up to 90 percent LTC)
Regional banks in heavy industrial markets with local expertise
Debt funds for value-add or transitional plays

key_features.lender_filter: Most mainstream banks decline; specialty lenders understand single-purpose buildings
key_features.environmental_overlay: Phase I always, Phase II common, potential remediation considerations
key_features.equipment_vs_real_property: Equipment allocation affects SBA eligibility and LTV basis
key_features.operator_credit_weight: Operator credit is more important than for standard industrial
key_features.top_markets: Vernon and City of Commerce in LA, Inland Empire, Detroit, Cleveland, Houston, Nashville

seo.meta_template: Manufacturing and heavy industrial financing in {city}. Specialty lender ecosystem, environmental and equipment underwriting, and why banks decline most of these deals.

programs.name: Industrial Bridge Financing
programs.description: Bridge financing for transitional industrial assets: acquisition of vacant or short-WALT warehouse and distribution space, lease-up of speculative development, last-mile conversion, and repositioning of older flex or manufacturing product ahead of a permanent take-out.
programs.typical_deal_range: $5M to $75M for single-asset and small-portfolio industrial
typical_stack: Bridge loan from a debt fund, mortgage REIT, or balance-sheet bank
Interest reserve sized to carry the asset through lease-up
Capital for tenant improvements, leasing commissions, and light repositioning
Exit to a life company, CMBS, or bank permanent loan at stabilization

key_features.rate_environment_2026: SOFR + 350 to 600 bps, floor rates common
key_features.typical_ltv_ltc: 70 to 80 percent LTC, 65 to 75 percent of stabilized value
key_features.prepayment: Open after a short lockout period
key_features.recourse_structure: Often non-recourse with bad-boy carve-outs; partial recourse on heavier lease-up risk
key_features.primary_lender_type: Debt funds, mortgage REITs, and regional balance-sheet banks

seo.meta_template: Industrial bridge financing in {city}. Lender ecosystem for warehouse and distribution lease-up, interest reserve sizing, repositioning capital, and permanent take-out sequencing.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.market_notes: Vernon, City of Commerce, Carson, and the LA industrial core represent some of the most valuable per-square-foot industrial real estate in the country. Supply is effectively capped by zoning and the Port of LA/Long Beach complex drives distribution demand.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies are extremely competitive for stabilized LA industrial with credit tenancy. CMBS active for $15M+ stabilized assets. Regional banks compete for owner-user and construction. Specialty lenders active in cold storage and manufacturing given Vernon's heavy industrial concentration.
cities.submarkets: Vernon, City of Commerce, Carson, San Pedro, Wilmington, Gardena, South Gate, Cudahy, Pico Rivera, Industry

cities.name: Phoenix
cities.market_notes: One of the fastest-growing industrial markets in the country. Strong institutional demand for Class A distribution in the Southwest Valley (Goodyear, Buckeye, Tolleson) and Southeast Valley. Massive e-commerce fulfillment buildout over the past 5 years.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies very active for stabilized Class A distribution. CMBS quoting tight spreads. National banks aggressive on construction. Data centers have become a major focus with significant capital deployment.
cities.submarkets: Southwest Valley (Goodyear, Buckeye, Tolleson), Southeast Valley (Chandler, Mesa), Sky Harbor, Deer Valley, North Phoenix

cities.name: Inland Empire
cities.market_notes: The largest industrial market in North America by square footage. Ontario, Rancho Cucamonga, Fontana, Moreno Valley, and Riverside are core distribution markets. Eastern IE (Moreno Valley, Beaumont) has seen massive big-box buildout tied to LA port distribution.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies compete aggressively for stabilized IE distribution. CMBS very active for $15M+ stabilized credit-tenant deals. Regional and national banks strong on construction. Specialty lenders active in IOS given the truck yard and container storage demand.
cities.submarkets: Ontario, Rancho Cucamonga, Fontana, Riverside, Moreno Valley, Perris, Jurupa Valley, Mira Loma, Eastvale, Beaumont

cities.name: Dallas
cities.market_notes: DFW is a top-three industrial market nationally. Strong institutional demand for Class A distribution in Alliance, Great Southwest, South Dallas, and DFW Airport submarkets. Texas tax environment and population growth driving continued demand.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies very competitive for Dallas industrial. CMBS active for stabilized. Regional Texas banks strong on construction and owner-user manufacturing. Data centers booming with North Texas hyperscale buildout.
cities.submarkets: Alliance, DFW Airport, Great Southwest, South Dallas, Stemmons, Northeast Dallas, East Dallas, Mesquite, Garland

cities.name: Houston
cities.market_notes: Houston industrial tied to energy, petrochemical, Port of Houston distribution, and food processing. Unique mix of Class A distribution alongside heavy industrial and manufacturing facilities serving the energy sector.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies active for distribution. Specialty lenders critical for energy-adjacent and petrochemical facilities. Regional banks strong in manufacturing and food processing. Cold storage has seen major buildout given Gulf Coast food distribution demand.
cities.submarkets: North Belt, Northwest Houston, Southwest Houston, North Houston, Sugar Land, Katy, Stafford, Pasadena, East Houston

cities.name: Atlanta
cities.market_notes: Southeast logistics hub serving the growing Southeast consumer market. Hartsfield-Jackson cargo volume, strong rail infrastructure, and interstate access drive distribution demand. South Atlanta and the I-20 West corridor are major Class A distribution submarkets.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Life insurance companies and CMBS very competitive for Atlanta distribution. Data centers have been major growth area. Regional Southeast banks competitive on construction. Cold storage and food processing active given the Southeast food distribution network.
cities.submarkets: South Atlanta, I-20 West, North Atlanta, Airport West, Stone Mountain, I-85 South, Henry County, Northwest Atlanta
